diagnoses.preserve: Training a configurable text-generating network on text datasets with a few lines of code, and the alternative of using a pretrained model.
diagnoses.problem: “Easily” and “quickly” promise effort and speed without conditions; combined with “any size and complexity,” they make the opening more promotional than informative.
diagnoses.quote: Easily train your own text-generating neural network of any size and complexity on any text dataset with a few lines of code, or quickly train on a text using a pretrained model.

diagnoses.preserve: The module description and the feature list that follows.
diagnoses.problem: “Many cool features” adds subjective praise immediately before the concrete features supply the useful information.
diagnoses.quote: with many cool features:

diagnoses.preserve: Attention-weighting and skip-embedding, and their stated benefits for training speed and model quality.
diagnoses.problem: “Modern” and “new” are undated novelty claims that add no architectural information beyond the named techniques.
diagnoses.quote: A modern neural network architecture which utilizes new techniques as attention-weighting and skip-embedding to accelerate training and improve model quality.

diagnoses.preserve: The CuDNN RNN implementation, its GPU training condition, and its speed advantage over typical LSTM implementations.
diagnoses.problem: “Powerful” and “massively” inflate the performance claim without a measurement; “speeds up training time” also muddles whether training becomes faster or its duration increases.
diagnoses.quote: Utilize a powerful CuDNN implementation of RNNs when trained on the GPU, which massively speeds up training time as opposed to typical LSTM implementations.

diagnoses.preserve: The included model can be trained on new texts and can generate text after a single pass of the input data.
diagnoses.problem: “Easily” asserts unspecified effort, while “appropriate text” leaves the claimed output quality undefined despite the concrete example below.
diagnoses.quote: The included model can easily be trained on new texts, and can generate appropriate text

diagnoses.preserve: Weights occupy 2 MB on disk and can be saved and loaded into a new textgenrnn instance.
diagnoses.problem: The explicit 2 MB size already supplies the useful evidence; “relatively small” adds an unspecified comparison and “easily” adds an unsupported ease judgment.
diagnoses.quote: The model weights are relatively small (2 MB on disk), and they can easily be saved and loaded into a new textgenrnn instance.

diagnoses.preserve: The surrounding advice to increase temperature significantly for creative output from extensively trained models.
diagnoses.problem: “So well” presents the need to adjust temperature as evidence of exceptional learning quality without explaining that inference.
diagnoses.quote: so well

diagnoses.preserve: Interactive mode lets users choose successive characters or words from the top N suggestions.
diagnoses.problem: This introductory sentence vaguely announces participation, then the next sentence explains the exact interaction; it adds no distinct instruction.
diagnoses.quote: It's also possible to get involved in how the output unfolds, step by step.

diagnoses.preserve: The user's ability to guide generated output and the accompanying reference.
diagnoses.problem: “It feels like you're the writer” repeats the human-participation pitch after the actual selection mechanism and example, adding a subjective experience claim.
diagnoses.quote: to the output; it feels like you're the writer!

diagnoses.preserve: The char-rnn attribution and the ability to work with very small text sequences.
diagnoses.problem: “A few modern optimizations” is vague, time-dependent framing; the small-sequence capability is the concrete distinction.
diagnoses.quote: with a few modern optimizations, such as the ability to work with very small text sequences.

diagnoses.preserve: All three layers feed attention; attention weights and averages temporal features; embeddings and the first LSTM have skip connections that aid backpropagation and prevent vanishing gradients.
diagnoses.problem: A long causal parenthesis packs the skip connections, backpropagation, and gradient benefit into the attention aggregation sentence, obscuring the distinction between data flow and training rationale.
diagnoses.quote: All three layers are then fed into an Attention layer to weight the most important temporal features and average them together (and since the embeddings + 1st LSTM are skip-connected into the attention layer, the model updates can backpropagate to them more easily and prevent vanishing gradients).

diagnoses.preserve: The output gives next-character probabilities for up to 394 characters, including uppercase, lowercase, punctuation, and emoji, with the vocabulary link retained.
diagnoses.problem: “That they are the next character” is an awkward delayed clause whose plural pronoun makes the probability mapping harder to parse.
diagnoses.quote: that they are the next character in the sequence, including uppercase characters, lowercase, punctuation, and emoji.

diagnoses.preserve: The text-only path benefits from decontextualized layers, with stated training-speed and quantitative and qualitative performance improvements over text-only training.
diagnoses.problem: “Piggy-back off” leaves the architectural relationship informal and imprecise, while “in all” and unquantified “much” burden the comparison with summary padding and emphasis.
diagnoses.quote: The text-only path can piggy-back off the decontextualized layers; in all, this results in much faster training and better quantitative and qualitative model performance than just training the model gien the text alone.

diagnoses.preserve: Training used hundreds of thousands of Reddit submission documents from varied subreddits, obtained via the linked BigQuery source.
diagnoses.problem: In “a very diverse variety,” “diverse” and “variety” repeat the same point, and “very” adds an unsupported degree.
diagnoses.quote: from a very

diagnoses.preserve: Pretraining is the stated basis for faster, more accurate fine-tuning and the possibility of learning relationships absent from the original dataset; retain the linked embedding example.
diagnoses.problem: “Much more robust ‘knowledge’” substitutes an anthropomorphic, unmeasured comparison for a clear account of the pretraining benefit, and “initially”/“in the end” add loose temporal framing.
diagnoses.quote: However, since the original pretrained network has a much more robust "knowledge" initially, the new textgenrnn trains faster and more accurately in the end, and can potentially learn new relationships not present in the original dataset

diagnoses.preserve: A planned web-based tensorflow.js implementation and the network's small size as its stated advantage.
diagnoses.problem: “Works especially well” does not identify what improves—feasibility, speed, or resource use—and presents an unspecified success claim inside a future plan.
diagnoses.quote: A web-based implementation using tensorflow.js (works especially well due to the network's small size)

diagnoses.preserve: Plans for positional context and multiple context labels.
diagnoses.problem: “More depth toward context” is an opaque umbrella phrase; the parenthetical already names the two concrete planned capabilities.
diagnoses.quote: More depth toward context (positional context + allowing multiple context labels)

diagnoses.preserve: A planned larger pretrained network, support for longer character sequences, and the intended improvements in language modeling and generated sentences.
diagnoses.problem: “A more indepth understanding of language” and “better generated sentences” are broad quality aspirations tangled into the concrete sequence-length capability, making the planned change harder to distinguish from its hoped-for benefits.
diagnoses.quote: A larger pretrained network which can accommodate longer character sequences and a more indepth understanding of language, creating better generated sentences.

diagnoses.preserve: Planned FP16 training on Volta/TPUs, conditional on sufficient Keras support.
diagnoses.problem: “Superfast” supplies promotional intensity without a benchmark or comparison.
diagnoses.quote: FP16 for superfast training on Volta/TPUs (once Keras has good support for it).

diagnoses.preserve: The conditional request for Patreon contributions, appreciation for them, and their support for the maintainer's creative work.
diagnoses.problem: “Will be put to good creative use” is an unspecified assurance that repeats the preceding explanation that Patreon supports the maintainer's projects.
diagnoses.quote: If you found this project helpful, any monetary contributions to the Patreon are appreciated and will be put to good creative use.
